The selected pages of this section cover how bad driving habits form from laziness, impatience, inattention, arrogance and ignorance, distracted driving, the five rules of defensive driving, attentiveness and scanning, driver and vehicle condition, trip planning, warning lamps, safety belts, what happens in a collision and protecting a baby in the car; they teach driving habits, attention, defensive driving, trip preparation and safety belts and say nothing about any examination; they state no exam name, question count, passing standard, format or time limit.

The run scope names the Hawaii Department of Transportation as the handbook issuer and the twenty twenty-three printing as the edition, but these pages carry no page-bound issuer or edition statement, so part A asserts no issuer or edition fact of its own.

Question count, passing standard, format and time limit for the class three knowledge test are not stated anywhere in this manual; every official exam fact stays unknown in this envelope and is never guessed.

Corpus note: this is stable teaching content printed in this twenty twenty-three edition, with the belt statistics stated only as printed and no annual-rewrite signal on these pages.
